Declan Rice celebrated Arsenal’s Premier League title triumph with an Instagram post calling back to his now famous line at the end of the Gunners’ April defeat by Manchester City.

Rice was pictured saying “it’s not over” to his captain Martin Odegaard at full-time in the 2-1 defeat which swung title-race momentum in favour of reigning champions City.

The moment of defiance was both hailed and mocked on social media, but Rice was proved right as the Gunners sealed their first Premier League title for 22 years following Tuesday night’s 1-1 draw between City and Bournemouth.

He posted: “I told you all… it’s done.”

Arsenal players had gathered at their London Colney training base to watch the Bournemouth game, and the full-time whistle at the Vitality Stadium brought wild celebrations from players and staff.

Meanwhile, thousands of Arsenal fans rushed to the Emirates Stadium to celebrate on the concourses outside the north London ground, singing and setting off fireworks.

Rice’s relentless running, pin-point set pieces and tireless tackling have been pivotal and have fully justified the record £105m the club spent ⁠on him in 2023.

Declan Rice has been instrumental in Arsenal’s glory ( Reuters )

Statistically, his influence has been immense. He ​has ⁠played in all but one of Arsenal’s league matches this season, scoring four goals, providing five assists and completing well over 2,100 passes with a near 90 per cent success rate.

Defensively, ⁠he has been perhaps even more crucial. His 70 tackles and 37 interceptions have combined with ​equally superb ⁠performances from teammates David Raya in ‌goal and centre back pairing Gabriel and William Saliba, to make the Arsenal defence the meanest in the league.

Manager Mikel Arteta was asked in January, after Rice had scored a crucial brace in ‌a tight 3-2 away win against Bournemouth, whether he thought ‌Rice’s attributes made him one of the best midfielders in the world.

“For me yes,” Arteta replied immediately. “Declan is constantly adding things to his game, he’s constantly adding things to his role in the team. I don’t see where he can stop.”

Arsenal will play Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on Sunday where they will receive the trophy, before turning their attentions to next weekend’s Champions League final against PSG.

additional reporting by Reuters

Tottenham Hotspur’s survival fight will go to the final day after they missed out on the chance to seal survival against Chelsea.

With West Ham two points behind and with just one game left, victory at Stamford Bridge would have made certain of a Premier League place next season for Spurs – and a draw would almost certainly have sufficed, too, given their vastly superior goal difference.

But having been beaten 2-1 by their London rivals, Roberto De Zerbi’s side face an anxious final day encounter with Everton with West Ham taking on Leeds simultaneously.

The situation might have been different, though, had a late penalty appeal been given by referee Stuart Attwell.

With a corner about to be taken, Attwell blew his whistle and brandished a yellow card in the direction of Chelsea’s Marc Cucurella, who appeared to wrestle Micky van de Ven to the floor.

The incident occurred in the 85th minute after Richarlison had halved the deficit for the visitors, and several Spurs players seemed to wonder why Attwell did not point to the penalty spot having deemed the incident worthy of a caution.

However, IFAB Law 12, which covers fouls and misconduct, clearly states that direct and indirect free-kicks, and penalty kickss, can only be awarded for offences committed in “when the ball is in play”. As the corner had not yet been delivered, as was determined by video assistant referee John Brooks, that was not the case in these circumstances.

Jell-O — long known for its bright rainbow of artificially colored gelatins — is getting a line of products made without synthetic colors or artificial sweeteners to meet increasing consumer demand for natural ingredients.

Kraft Heinz Co. on Tuesday unveiled Jell-O Simply, a line of pre-made gelatin that the company said is made with fruit juice and has at least 25% less sugar than the regular version.

The ready-to-eat range now available in stores comes in three flavors -- orange, raspberry lemonade and blueberry. Kathryn O’Brien, Kraft Heinz’s head of marketing for desserts, said the products are colored using vegetable juice, fruit juice and an extract derived from turmeric roots.

Kraft Heinz said it would expand the Jell-O Simply brand in August to include vanilla and chocolate instant pudding and banana and strawberry gelatin mixes, part of the food and beverage company's broader transition to natural ingredients.

Consumers are actively looking for foods with natural ingredients and less sugar, Kraft Heinz said Tuesday. That has taken a toll on products with artificial colors and flavors like Jell-O. Industrywide sales of pre-made gelatin have fallen 21% over the last four years, while unit sales of gelatin mix have fallen 4%, according to market research company NielsenIQ.

Food brands have also been under pressure from the federal government to remove artificial colors from packaged foods. In the waning days of the Biden administration, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration banned a dye known as Red 3 from the U.S. food supply. A few months later, Trump administration officials urged food makers to voluntarily phase out other petroleum-based artificial colors.

Some retailers are also pressing companies to remove artificial ingredients. Target said in February that it would stop selling cereals containing synthetic colors by this summer.

Last summer, Kraft Heinz pledged to remove artificial dyes from its U.S. products by 2027. At the time, the company said 90% of its U.S. products didn’t contain synthetic dyes. Kraft Heinz removed artificial colors from its macaroni and cheese in 2016, for example. But they remain in brands like Jell-O, Kool-Aid and Crystal Light.

O’Brien described Jell-O Simply as a “meaningful evolution” for the 125-year-old brand. It still jiggles and tastes like Jell-O, she said, and it’s still vibrantly colored.

“We know families are looking for treats that strike the right balance between great taste and ingredients they can feel good about, and they don’t want to sacrifice the brands they know and love to get there,” O’Brien said in a statement.

O'Brien said the Jell-O Simply brand is a permanent addition to the company's portfolio and will remain even when artificial colors are removed from the rest of the Jell-O lineup next year. Regular Jell-O products might contain artificial sweeteners, for example.

Like Jell-O, Jell-O Simply's primary ingredient is gelatin, a colorless, flavorless substance derived from animal collagen. Collagen is sourced from the skin, bones and connective tissues of animals like cows, pigs or fish, according to the Michigan State University Center for Research on Ingredient Safety.

As with some other natural products — like Lay's Simply Cheetos — consumers will pay slightly more for Jell-O Simply. A Jell-O Simply pre-made four-pack is $3.99, or 46 cents more than a regular Jell-O four-pack, the company said.

News.title: Spurs’ relegation fears extend to final day after narrow loss at Chelsea
News.content:
In the north, their oldest rivals celebrated a historic Premier League title, while in the west, Chelsea did what they almost always do when Tottenham Hotspur visit Stamford Bridge. Anguish all over London for Spurs again this night – the securing of their Premier League status now down to the last day of the season on Sunday.

This was another night of missed opportunities, the 17th defeat of the season from hell while 16 places above Arsenal claimed their seventh league title since Spurs won their last in 1961. But for now the unbearable weight of all that history will have to wait because there is still a good chance that Spurs will be playing in the Football League next season. They have to take a point at home to Everton on Sunday to be safe from relegation – at a stadium where they have won just twice all season.

Beaten by Chelsea, a side that won for the first time in eight Premier League games – Spurs left the pitch at Chelsea asking referee for Stuart Attwell for more time. But time is running out. They lead West Ham in 18th place by two points and a win for the Nuno Espirito Santo’s men at home to Leeds United will be enough if Spurs fail to take a point.

News.title: Man City’s title dream ends with draw at Bournemouth
News.content:
“One more year”, chanted the Manchester City fans at the departing Pep Guardiola, but the looming reality is just one more match. And, with this 1-1 draw at Bournemouth confirming Arsenal’s first Premier League title since 2004, that match has been rendered a sporting irrelevance.

Yes, those at City will rightly make it a celebration of the footballing revolution that Guardiola has overseen during an extraordinary, era-defining decade in English football, but the chance to take Arsenal to the wire has gone.

Six Premier League titles in 10 years will be the final tally for Guardiola, a manager whose place among the all-time greats of English football is secure, even if this chapter will only be complete once the outcome of the 115 Premier League charges against City is known.

City never really looked like winning here against a Bournemouth team who took a deserved first-half lead through Junior Kroupi before Erling Haaland’s 95th minute equaliser provided just a fleeting hope that they could secure the win that would take the title race to the final day. Guardiola crossed the pitch to applaud the City fans on the final whistle but, after winning two domestic cups this year, he cut a resigned figure as the fans made their emotional last plea for him to stay.

News.title: Nasdaq plunges as US bond sell-off deepens
News.content:
Stocks fell sharply on Wall Street as inflation fears pushed up the cost of US government borrowing to its highest level since 2007.

The Nasdaq Composite sank by as much as 1.7pc as it was swept up in a global bond market sell-off driven by concerns over the war in the Middle East.

Tensions remain high over whether a peace deal can be reached between the US and Iran to end the conflict that has sent energy prices soaring.

Oil had fallen on Tuesday, with Brent crude down 1pc below $111 a barrel, after Donald Trump said he had held off launching a new offensive in hopes of striking a deal.

But Iran’s army has warned that it would “open new fronts” against the United States if it resumes attacks.

Concerns over an extended conflict, and higher energy prices, have steadily pushed up the cost of US government borrowing during the war.

The yield on 30-year US Treasury bonds – a guide to the interest rate it pays to borrow money – has climbed from 4.61pc at the end of February to nearly 5.2pc, the highest since 2007.

Steve Sosnick of Interactive Brokers said: “After pretending this was not a problem, I think (the market) has now decided that higher yields are in fact a problem.

“But we aren’t seeing panic or anything like that.”

It comes as Britain awaits official inflation figures on Wednesday that will show how the Iran war is affecting prices.

On Tuesday, petrol prices rose to their highest level since the start of the war, with a litre of unleaded costing 158.52p.

News.title: The best spa hotels in Devon
News.content:
All our reviewers are either resident destination experts or travel writers that specialise in hotels. Often they will have stayed at a hotel many times and so can see how it has changed for better or worse over the years. They know what makes a great hotel in that particular destination and will compare it contextually against local competition. When our reviewers first visit a hotel, they stay for at least one night, eat one meal in addition to breakfast and will experience all of the facilities on offer. Whichever category of room they stay in, they will see the entry-level rooms in order to assess them.

After their stay, our reviewers then give the hotel six scores out of 10, rating its location, style and character, service and facilities, rooms, food and drink, and value for money. The average of these scores then determines the overall score. Our experts then select reviews for curated lists like this – the best hotels in a particular destination for families, for instance – together with the Telegraph Hotels team.

News.title: Youth unemployment hits 11-year high as Labour tax rises bite
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Youth unemployment has surged to an 11-year high as Labour’s tax raids hit the jobs market. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

What happened overnight

Markets steadied overnight after Donald Trump said he had postponed planned strikes on Iran, raising hopes that a fresh diplomatic push could avert a wider Middle East conflict and further disruption to global oil supplies.

Oil prices fell back from earlier highs after the US president said Gulf allies, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, had asked Washington to “hold off” military action while negotiations continued. The retreat in crude prices helped Wall Street pare losses and pushed Treasury yields lower.

Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 index was down 1.75pc at 58,475.90, dragged lower by technology stocks as investors worried about rising oil prices and higher global bond yields. South Korea’s Kospi was also weaker after recent record highs, with chipmakers under pressure ahead of key Nvidia earnings.

News.title: Uganda bans hugs and handshakes as two cases of Ebola are confirmed
News.content:
Uganda has banned handshakes and hugs after two cases of Ebola were confirmed in the country amid a major outbreak in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Diana Atwine, Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Health, on Tuesday urged the public to follow preventive measures including the temporary ban on handshakes, hugging and unnecessary physical contact.

“We are saying people must stop greeting… this [virus] relies upon physical contact,” she told a press conference.

Uganda’s health ministry has also advised the public to wash their hands with soap, use alcohol-based hand sanitisers and report any symptoms including fever, vomiting or bleeding immediately.

The two cases confirmed in Uganda are linked to the outbreak in the DRC, where 130 people have died and at least 500 people are believed to have been infected with the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

One of the cases, a 59-year-old man, died on Thursday, while the second patient remains under isolation and close monitoring, Ugandan health officials say.

Three countries in Southeast Asia have begun tightening their borders in response to the outbreak in recent days.

Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia have all increased their surveillance of hospitals and airports, whilst watching border quarantine checkpoints closely.

Thailand’s Department of Disease Control (DDC) and Vietnam’s Ministry of Health have both issued guidance urging those returning from affected areas to monitor their health for symptoms of Ebola, while Indonesia’s health ministry has said that suspected cases will immediately be referred to designated hospitals.

News.title: The best humidifiers to hydrate dry skin and soothe allergies, tested
News.content:
Indoor air that’s too dry can irritate skin, cause asthma symptoms, sore throats and even cracked lips. Adding moisture back with a humidifier may help.

They’re useful in summer, when fans and air conditioners dry the air, and winter, when heating and dehumidifiers do the same. I know how shifts in temperature can leave my son’s skin feeling uncomfortably dry (not to mention my own), so I’m always looking for ways to manage ot.

I tested 10 of the most popular humidifier brands, including Dyson, Humio and Meaco, to see if they’d help. Incidentally, my house plants have flourished thanks to the added moisture in the air. Prices vary from about £60 to nearly £700, depending on the device you choose.

You can read my reviews further down, followed by some advice on how to use humidifiers. Here’s a quick look at my top five:

The best humidifiers: At a glance

How to choose the best humidifier

“Many adults suffering with asthma, eczema or allergies choose to buy humidifiers,” says Dr Semiya Aziz, general practitioner and founder of Say GP. “However, it’s important to do your research before purchasing. For example, cool-mist humidifiers may ease a stuffy nose during a cold, whereas a heated humidified air doesn’t seem to have the same result and may be of no benefit.”

Sports.title: Lioness Lauren James becomes a millionaire after her wealth soars off pitch
Sports.content:
LOADED LIONESS Lioness Lauren James becomes a millionaire after her wealth soars off pitch

LIONESS Lauren James has scored big off the pitch and is a millionaire, company records reveal.

Equity in her firm, L James Ventures Ltd, rose by £400,000 to £987,223 for the year to last May 31, records show.



The striker — said to be on £350,000 a year at Chelsea — has lucrative sponsorship deals with firms including Nike, Barclays and Sure.

She paid £600,000 for an investment property and has more than £500,000 in the bank.



Lauren, 24, who has 38 England caps, paid £180,000 in tax, suggesting she earned £700,000.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola breaks silence on Man City exit after draw against Bournemouth
Sports.content:
PEP GUARDIOLA didn’t confirm that he is leaving Manchester City at the end of the season.

The Sky Blues boss was quizzed again on his future following tonight’s 1-1 draw away to Bournemouth – a result that handed Arsenal their first title in 22 years.





That came just a day after reports emerged claiming he will leave the Etihad this summer.

While Guardiola insisted he still has one year left on his contract, he stopped short of giving any firm commitment beyond that.

Asked directly what the next chapter of his story would be at City, Guardiola said: “I would say that I have one more year of my contract, and the conversations I have many, many years – whatever you announce… during the competition is a bad result, and the first person I have to talk to is my Chairman.

“When the season is finished we will see, and afterwards we will take the decision.



“I have one more year on my contract, and I won’t tell you here because I have to talk with my Chairman, my players, my staff because when we play for FA Cup, for qualification to the Champions League, and we play for the Premier League, just one thing in my mind is the focus – and that’s to being the team to the highest point. That’s what we’ve done.

“I’m the happiest man on the planet to be in this club, this club is extraordinary.

“Of course in the moment this season is over for us, we want to arrive in the last game to our fans. And I know they will come and in ten seasons they have been really good in many moments and that is what we have to do until the end.”

The result saw City’s title hopes in ruins.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Pegged back by Eli Junior Kroupi’s strike in the 38th minute, the Citizens hit back in stoppage time through Erling Haaland but it wasn’t enough to save them.

While we haven’t yet heard it from the horse’s mouth, the next few days will all fuel speculation that Sunday’s game at home to Aston Villa could be Guardiola’s last in the Etihad dugout.

Asked before the game whether the speculation had affected him personally or disrupted preparations, Guardiola bluntly replied: “Zero. Absolutely zero!”

Reports suggest that should he leave, his former assistant and Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca is set to replace him.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2 Tottenham 1: Spurs’ relegation battle goes down to final day after Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos goals
Sports.content:
WE are going the distance.

Tottenham suffering yet another defeat at Stamford Bridge means the dropzone scrap with West Ham extends to the final day.





Enzo Fernandez’s early pearler and an Andrey Santos strike did the damage.

Though a late Richarlison tap-in added some late, faint Spurs hope which ultimately came to nothing, in spite of a bonkers final ten minutes where the desperate visitors chucked everything they could at Chelsea.

It was hard to work out who enjoyed the result more: the gleeful Blues supporters revelling in their rivals’ suffering – or Hammers hardman fan Ross Kemp who was also in attendance here.

Now we are set for a dramatic finale befitting of an Eastenders Christmas special to find out which of these London neighbours will be slinging their hook from the Premier League.

Spurs followers know that misery in Chelsea’s backyard is as certain as death, taxes and a Mitchell brothers barney.

Their barely believable run at Stamford Bridge now stands at: Played 41, won ONE.

And yet they had gone into this clash feeling their luck could actually change for once, given the new life that Roberto De Zerbi has breathed back into their survival bid.

The Italian had presided over a four-game unbeaten streak which, coupled with Nuno Espirito Santo’s Irons losing three on the bounce, meant they needed only a point here to stay up.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That was due to the two-point gap to 18th-placed West Ham being effectively three because of Spurs’ vastly superior goal difference.

It remains the case heading into Sunday when Tottenham host Everton and the Hammers entertain Leeds.

But it could have been done and dusted from the North Londoners perspective had they not felt that familiar sinking feeling in SW6 last night.

In theory, Chelsea were there for the taking, having lost nine of their last 11, including Saturday’s FA Cup final against Manchester City, and with interim Calum McFarlane still holding the fort.



That is, of course, until the exciting Xabi Alonso takes over in July.

But, as ever, the Blues found a way to lift themselves against their North London neighbours and keep their European qualification pursuit alive.

Though Bournemouth’s point against Manchester City – which gifted Arsenal the title – means the slim chance of Alonso bossing the club in the Champions League next term is now over.

Spurs started pretty well, with Jorrel Hato almost poking a clearance past his own keeper and Mathys Tel crashing a header against the post.

But nothing ever seems to go right for them at this ground – to the point where De Zerbi even addressed the atrocious record with his troops on Tuesday morning – and so it proved again.



With just 18 minutes on the clock, Fernandez suddenly had acres of space outside the Spurs box to let fly from 25 yards.

Keeper Antonin Kinsky got nowhere near the ball which dipped and swerved its way into the near corner.

That sparked a chant of “Tottenham Hotspur, it’s happening again” from the Matthew Harding Stand.



You wondered if the away players heard the taunt and became affected by it because they seemed to wilt at that point.

Fernandez almost had a second when he blasted a free-kick onto the crossbar from an acute angle.

Confidence was hardly boosted either when the home fans sang “that’s why you’re going down” on two occasions.

First was when Randal Kolo Muani miscued a cross badly out of play, before Mathys Tel got the same treatment for smashing a woeful shot into Row Z.

Spurs were drifting and De Zerbi knew it, so prepared to make a triple substitution including James Maddison in the 67th minute.



But as the trio waited, stripped and ready to come on, Chelsea scored again.

Muani gifted the ball to Cole Palmer, sparking a move which saw Pedro Neto cross for Enzo, who cut it back for Santos to roll into the corner.

It was a hammer blow that looked to have KO’d Spurs chances in this game.



Yet De Zerbi has added a more resilient streak and, with 17 minutes to go, sub Pape Sarr’s backheeled shot squirmed its way to Richarlison who slotted home.

It looked like it would get even better when Maddison was suddenly free deep inside the box, but his close-range shot was blocked by Hato.

From the resulting corner, mayhem ensued as Marc Cucurella wrestled an irate Micky van de Ven to the ground and was booked.

But NO penalty was given because technically the ball was not in play.

The madness continued as Liam Delap appeared to catch Djed Spence in the face with an elbow but escaped with a caution.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

It was a fresh update of the Battle of the Bridge ten years on from the original instalment.

Now Tottenham must show battle and bottle on the final day against Everton to ensure they have a league fixture at Chelsea next term.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Fernandez and Santos on song but Delap not good enough to wear shirt against Tottenham
Sports.content:
CHELSEA and Tottenham’s storied rivalry had a new chapter written in it as the Blues sent Spurs’ relegation battle to the final day.

An Enzo Fernandez stunner from range broke the deadlock, with the Argentine winger pulling out an, interesting, mobile phone celebration.





The Blues were dominant for most of the first half, with Palmer going close and Fernandez rattling the bar from a free-kick.

And home fans relished chanting “that’s why you’re going down” every time a visitor in yellow fired over or wide.

Spurs’ only chance of any real quality was a Mathys Tel header that caressed the inside of the post.

News of Arsenal winning the title spread misery among both sets of fans at the Bridge, but Chelsea supporters got some light relief when Andrey Santos made it 2-0 in the second half.



Spurs didn’t give up, with Richarlison finding the back of the net after a clever Pape Matar Sarr backheel inside the box, but it wasn’t enough to save them on the night.

This is how SunSport’s Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

ROBERT SANCHEZ – 6

With Chelsea eyeing up a keeper in Robin Roefs for the summer, Sanchez has got a point to prove between now and the end of the season, especially with the impending return of Mike Penders from his loan, too.

He kept the Blues in it at 0-0 when he got down low to Tel’s header off the post, but couldn’t do anything to stop Richarlison from getting Spurs back in the game.



Was dependable on the whole.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 5

Tonight was a massive chance for the 19-year-old to impress at right-back, with Malo Gusto out and Reece James on the bench.

He progressed the ball relatively well down the right, and wasn’t caused heaps of problems by Tel and Udogie on the Spurs left, although he was a little slow to get to his man.

WESLEY FOFANA – 5

Wasn’t made to struggle too much by Richarlison on the end of any Spurs crosses going into the middle, and the Frenchman was largely dominant at the back.



He played Richarlison onside as Spurs got a goal back.

JORREL HATO – 7

It’s been a successful season for Hato, with plenty of encouraging signs in the last few games in particular for the youngster.

A nervy loose touch almost put the ball in the back of his own net within the first five minutes, but he soon improved and progressed the ball out nicely from the back.

Is well deserving of a spot in Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea XI next season for my money, and will have a bright future here thanks to his versatility and composure.

Made a massive block to deny Maddison at the death.



MARC CUCURELLA – 5

Was progressing high up the pitch for Chelsea on the left, as he is expected to do under Xabi Alonso if he is still here next season.

He was solid defensively against Kolo Muani, who looked a bag of nerves more often than not on the ball, but it was his poor header out from the back that led to Spurs finding a way back into the game.

ANDREY SANTOS – 8

With Reece James on the bench and Enzo Fernandez higher up, tonight represented a chance for Santos to prove why it was a mistake for Carlo Ancelotti to leave him out of Brazil‘s World Cup squad.

It’s not been the season he will have hoped for when he arrived in the summer, but tonight was one of his better showings, with some strong tackles and an ability to keep things ticking in midfield.



His left-footed stroke into the back of the net capped off a good night for the Brazilian.

MOISES CAICEDO – 6

Caicedo did what he had to do tonight, and did it well.

Nonstop in the Blues midfield, he made life really difficult for Conor Gallagher, and progressed the ball nicely too, never doing too much with it at his feet.

COLE PALMER – 3

It feels like forever since we’ve seen Cole Palmer at his unstoppable best.



Keen for a spot on the plane to the World Cup, and to impress new manager Xabi Alonso, this game was Palmer’s penultimate chance to impress before the summer.

He stroked a shot into the right palm of Kinsky within the first 15 minutes, and failed to do much more than that despite some clever touches.

Needs the summer off, for me.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 9

His position in this Chelsea team has been one of the most interesting to keep an eye on since Liam Rosenior was sacked, and he flirted with a move to Real Madrid.



His stunning opener from outside the box was too good for Kinsky, and would’ve certainly caught the attention of Xabi Alonso, but his mobile phone celebration would have too…

It would’ve been interesting to see how he celebrated when he rattled the crossbar minutes later from a free-kick.

Turned nothings into somethings for his side, with a neat assist for Andrey Santos too.

PEDRO NETO – 7

The Chelsea winger will take the assist for Fernandez’s goal, but it was a simple pass for the midfielder to do all the work from there.



His involvement in the second won’t earn him any G/A, but it was a brilliantly swept cross into Fernandez, who setup Santos to finish.

He smelled blood on Destiny Udogie after that, and went for him until the end.

LIAM DELAP – 2

One Premier League goal, that is all Chelsea have got out of Liam Delap for £30million this season – his biggest cheer of the night came when he won a foul from Micky Van de Ven.

Not good enough to end Chelsea’s ‘number 9 curse’, and not fit to wear the Chelsea shirt.

Gave Udogie an elbow at the end for good measure and was lucky to stay on the pitch.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

SUBS:

TREVOH CHALOBAH (JOSH ACHEAMPONG, 74) – 5

Didn’t make much of an impact in terms of stability at the back for Chelsea, but didn’t make any errors either.

MAMADOU SARR (WESLEY FOFANA, 81) – 5

It felt like forever since Sarr had played for Chelsea, but he was decent when he came on.

DARIO ESSUGO (COLE PALMER, 88) – N/A

LIAM DELAP (SHIM MHEUKA, 88) – N/A

ALEJANDRO GARNACHO (PEDRO NETO, 88) – N/A

Sports.title: Arsenal stars go wild and dance at training ground as they win Premier League title after watching Man City slip up
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’s stars gathered together at the club’s training ground to celebrate their title win.

The Gunners’ win over Burnley on Monday meant anything but a win for Manchester City the following day would confirm their status as champions.





And Pep Guardiola‘s men could not deliver, falling to a 1-1 draw on the south coast to dash their hopes of any final-day drama.

Mikel Arteta‘s decision to gather his stars at Colney to watch the match paid off as the team celebrated their momentous achievement together.

Declan Rice shared a look into the room, as he uploaded a snap with his team-mates to his Instagram account.

He captioned the post, showing several members of the team posing and grinning: “I told you all.. it’s done.”

Former Chelsea star Alexandre Pato and pop star Jess Glynne were among the stars to congratulate the star in the replies to the post.

Eli Junior Kroupi scored midway through the second half to stun Guardiola and Co at the Vitality Stadium.

The Spaniard tried everything as he made four attacking changes in hopes of hunting down two goals to flip the tie.

But he could only manage one, a consolation goal thumped in by Erling Haaland.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It is not the end he would have hoped for if he follows through on his plans to depart the club at the end of the season.



But for his former protege, the momentous occasion feels like just the beginning.

Arsenal fans descended on the Emirates to celebrate their big day, with the revelry spilling out of the pubs of North London and on to the streets.

It has been a long road for the side, having let a comfortable league lead turn into a gritty scrap with City at the top of the table.

Sports.title: The ‘real reason’ behind Pep Guardiola stepping down as Man City manager and why door is still open for England job
Sports.content:
AS he prowled Wembley Stadium’s touchline at the weekend, Pep Guardiola leapt, kicked and wildly gesticulated as if every intense emotion would influence the game.

Anyone watching the ­Manchester City boss’s elation at winning the FA Cup Final against Chelsea on Saturday would not have doubted his total commitment to the club.





But today the Premier League is shaken following the announcement that one of the greatest managers of all time is packing his bags.

Pep won 17 major trophies during his decade-long reign over the sky blue half of Manchester, including landing an astounding six Premier League titles, the Champions League trophy and three FA Cups.

The Spaniard’s departure from City has been rumoured for weeks, with suggestions that he wants to reconcile with his estranged wife, who returned to his home city of Barcelona nearly seven years ago. None of his three children live in the UK, and Pep is reportedly lonely.

The shock of his exit will reverberate well beyond the Etihad Stadium.

Pep not only built a dominant City side, he also helped Manchester’s 30-year transformation into a thriving metropolis, and showed the world that the Premier League was the pinnacle of the ­beautiful game.

No longer did the top talents such as goal-scoring machine Erling Haaland, want to go to Spain.

They needed to be here to prove themselves among the Prem’s elite.

Pep also brought much-needed style to football, dressing elegantly in a turtleneck top and smart slacks for much of this season.





His close friendship with Oasis brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher, outspoken political views and wry sense of ­humour demonstrated that there is much more to the 55-year-old manager than just tactical nous.

England legend Alan Shearer paid tribute to Pep, saying: “What a man — what a ­manager.

“He’s brought huge, huge ­success to Manchester City in his own way, in his own style.

“He’s a lovely guy, certainly down to earth. He’s always been very amicable, very open and always willing to have a conversation. He’s been one of the best, if not the best, we’ve ever seen.

“We didn’t think anyone would get near Sir Alex Ferguson, but he has without a doubt, and some will argue that he’s even better.”

A debate is sure to rage about whether Pep is on a par with former Manchester United manager Sir Alex, who won 13 Premier League titles, two Champions ­Leagues and five FA Cups for the red half of the city.

Fergie had a tougher start, having to turn round a failing side while Pep inherited a winning one, but the United boss achieved that haul over 27 years rather than just ten.

Whatever the merits of these two legends, no one can question Guardiola’s indelible impact.



Before he joined City in 2016, Pep was the footie manager every club in the world wanted.

Having become the youngest boss to win the Champions League with Barcelona in 2009, he then took charge of German champions Bayern Munich in 2013.

That appeared to be a blow to City’s oil-rich owner Sheikh ­Mansour, who had appointed Pep’s pal Txiki Begiristain as director of football a year earlier in a bid to lure his dream target to Manchester.

But Txiki, a former director of football at Barcelona, built an incredible behind-the-scenes operation that ­persuaded Pep of City’s unmatched ambitions.

And with the team having lifted the Premier League trophy in 2012 and 2014, the squad had the winning mentality Guardiola required.

On top of that, Manchester was a city on the up.

Spearheaded by former council leader Howard Bernstein, the centre had been dramatically remodelled after the IRA bombed the Arndale shopping centre in 1996.

The 2002 Commonwealth Games bequeathed the Etihad Stadium, trams knitted once-disconnected areas together, “Manchattan” tower blocks shot up and the BBC’s MediaCity in Salford brought TV stars north.



Pep turbocharged that change.

With his striking good looks, easy charm and fashion sense, everyone wanted to be like him.

A lot of his impeccable taste was due to his wife Cristina, 52, who he met when she worked in her parents’ clothes shop in Barcelona.

Every season Pep would tweak his look. Whether he was wearing a full three-piece suit with tie, rockers T-shirt or flat cap, fans soon took to copying him.

It was a refreshing change from the club tracksuits worn by most footie bosses.

His withering sense of humour will also be missed.

When a reporter asked why he speaks to his players on the pitch, he responded: “I do it for the cameras. For my ego.

“I’m the most famous person on the team. I need the cameras to go to sleep with incredible satisfaction.” Another time he poked fun at his reputation by saying: “I don’t like when Erling Haaland scores three goals and all the highlights are for him. I’m so jealous.”

Most managers tend to steer clear of politics, because it is frowned upon by football’s governing bodies.

Not Pep. He speaks his mind.



The City boss was fined £20,000 by the FA for wearing a yellow ribbon in solidarity with the Catalan ­politicians locked up for backing independence from Spain.

He also described the war in Gaza as “genocide” and criticised the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency in the United States.

That has led his detractors to suggest Pep is being a hypocrite, because City is bankrolled by the United Arab Emirates, which has been accused of human rights abuses.

Fans don’t tend to worry about such controversies when the team is playing well — and Pep’s team have rarely been anything other than brilliant.

In 2018 they won the Premier League with a record 100 points and two years later they secured the domestic treble by winning the FA Cup, League Cup and ­Premier League.

What Mansour wanted most was for City to be the best in Europe. Pep delivered that in 2023 in Istanbul in an incredible night by beating Inter Milan in the Champions League final.

After that, many felt the Spaniard would depart on a high.

It was a surprise to many that he signed a two-year contract extension in November 2024.



That was followed by a tough season, where Pep scratched his head so anxiously during games that it started to bleed.

There was also an uncharacteristic outburst when he swore at autograph hunters.

Shortly afterwards, in January 2025, it was revealed that he had split from his wife Cristina who he ­married in 2014 and had been with for 35 years.

This ­season didn’t start well either, and questions were again raised as to whether Pep was losing his touch.

But City won the League Cup and FA Cup, while keeping up the pressure at the top of the table.

Earlier this month, Oasis frontman Liam responded to rumours that his friend Pep was quitting.

The City fan wrote on X: “It’s funny that, as I’ve just got off the phone with him and he’s said the opposite.”

Whether the singer had spoken to Pep or not is unclear, but in public the manager kept insisting he was going to see out his final year of his contract next season.

That seemed unlikely to some observers, given that he was looking to buy a £13.5million property in ­Barcelona close to his wife’s home. Last spring there were reports in Spain that Cristina and Pep were trying to rekindle their relationship, even though the divorce was still proceeding.

Whether they do get back together or not, it is certain that the workaholic star will finally take a rest.



How long that lasts will depend on what offers come his way.

Pep has made it clear in the past that he won’t return to club football if he leaves City.

In 2024 he said: “The thought of starting off somewhere else, with all the process of the training and so on . . . no, no, no. Maybe a national team but that’s different.”

That leaves the door open for him to manage England.

With any luck, this won’t be adios, but see you soon.

Sports.title: Football coach who secretly filmed his women players undressing in changing rooms for years is slapped with lifetime ban
Sports.content:
FOOTIE PEST Football coach who secretly filmed his women players undressing in changing rooms for years is slapped with lifetime ban

A FOOTBALL coach has been slapped with a lifetime ban after he was caught secretly filming women and girls undressing – and posting the footage online.

Petr Vlachovsky, 43, was convicted of filming 14 players in changing rooms and showers over a four year period.





He was banned from coaching for five years and given a suspended one-year prison sentence last year after he was convicted in the Czech Republic.

Now, Uefa‘s Control, Ethics and Disciplinary Body (CEDB), has slapped Vlachovsky with a ban “from exercising any football-related activity for life”.

Vlachovsky coached girls and women at Czech side 1. FC Slovacko for almost 15 years before he was caught.

Vlachovsky’s youngest victim at the club was 17 years old and the oldest was 25.



The 43-year-old was arrested when cops found the covertly filmed footage online, in September 2023.

Police also found that the coach was in possession of child sexual abuse material.

Convicted pervert Vlachovsky had previously coached the Czech Republic’s women’s Under-19s team – he was even once voted the best women’s coach in the country.

After his conviction and five-year coaching ban, Czech players called for his punishment to be increased.



Uefa launched an investigation and found that Vlachovsky had breached rules on indecent behaviour and brought football into disrepute.

As well as giving him a lifetime ban from “football-related activity”, the CEDB wrote to Fifa to ask them to extend the ban internationally.

Victims told Seznam Zpravy that the secret filming had left them scared to sleep at night and anxious to go out in public.

Kristýna Janků said: “The camera must have been miniature, we didn’t see it at all and it never occurred to us that he could do something like that. He had it very well thought out.”

Alena Pěčková added: “Wherever I went, whether it was a public gym or another environment, a warning light would go off in my head and I would keep checking to see if there was a camera somewhere.



“I also started having problems with the way I saw my body. I just felt disgusted in some way.”

Players’ union boss Alex Phillips, who heads up Fifpro, told the Guardian that Vlachovsky’s case was “the tip of the iceberg”.

He said players often don’t know how to report concerns.

Fifpro said: “This outcome sends a strong and necessary message that abusive and inappropriate behaviour has no place in football.

“Safeguarding the wellbeing of players must remain a priority at every level.”

Sports.title: Granit Xhaka's message to Arsenal during title celebrations speaks volumes
Sports.content:
Granit Xhaka's message to Arsenal during title celebrations speaks volumes

Arsenal have been crowned Premier League champions and former Gunners captain Granit Xhaka has sent manager Mikel Arteta a heartfelt congratulations message

View 2 Images Granit Xhaka of Sunderland has sent a message to Arsenal (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Granit Xhaka has paid tribute to his former club Arsenal following their Premier League title win. The Gunners have secured the title after Manchester City's stalemate with Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium on Tuesday evening.

‌



As the final whistle sounded on the south coast, the Sunderland midfielder posted an image of himself alongside Mikel Arteta from their days together at the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Xhaka, who spent seven years at Arsenal, lifting two FA Cups and two Community Shields, credited the title success to the Spaniard's dedication.

‌



On his Instagram story, the Switzerland international said: "A special team, great players, and a club that never stopped believing but this is all because of you, Mikel. To everyone who doubted you, give this man and this coach the respect he deserves. Congratulations to the whole @arsenal family."

Declan Rice delivers perfect message as Arsenal players celebrate winning title READ MORE :

Arsene Wenger delivers Champions message as Arsenal end 22-year wait READ MORE :

Xhaka faced some criticism throughout his stint in the Premier League, though he left on a positive note. During his final campaign, the Swiss midfielder was instrumental as Arsenal launched their first genuine title bid under Arteta.

Despite his efforts, Xhaka fell just short of guiding the Gunners to silverware, with Manchester City retaining their status as English champions for a third consecutive season. In an interview with German publication NZZ am Sonntag, he revealed precisely why he opted to sign for Bayer Leverkusen when he did.

‌



The former Arsenal captain said: "I didn't come to Leverkusen as a boss, but because I was looking for a new challenge. I felt like my time at Arsenal was over for me after seven years in London.

"I came here as an experienced player and person. The other players see that I can give them something of what I have learned. That's part of my role here.

View 2 Images Arsenal players celebrated winning the title at the club's training ground

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"It was sometimes written that I was coming back to Germany because of my wife. That’s not the truth. Like me, she was very happy in London. I made the decision solely as a footballer and athlete.

"I came to a top club in Germany that has a plan and wants to achieve something. Of course, the change was easier for us because, like me, we used to live in Düsseldorf and it is close to Monchengladbach, where my wife grew up."

‌



When quizzed on the contrasts between Arsenal and Leverkusen, Xhaka responded: "You can only see what it’s really like if you can train here every day and be there.

"You can work in peace at Bayer Leverkusen, there is no chaos, other clubs are more in focus. This is an advantage. At Arsenal, the pressure is different.

"But we have high ambitions because we know that we have enormous potential in the team. If we keep working like this and keep our feet on the ground, we can achieve something."

Article continues below

The 33-year-old spent two years at Leverkusen, playing a key role as Xabi Alonso guided the club to an unbeaten Bundesliga triumph. Last summer, Xhaka made his return to English football, helping Sunderland avoid relegation back to the Championship.

Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola's message to Arsenal's title heroes speaks volumes about Man City boss

Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years after Pep Guardiola's Manchester City could only manage a draw away to Bournemouth

View 3 Images Man City boss Pep Guardiola after his side's draw at Bournemouth

Mikel Arteta's Arsenal heroes were crowned champions after Manchester City finally surrendered the race for the title.

‌



The Arsenal squad celebrated at the club’s training ground after doing a late session and then watched Bournemouth win the title for them.

‌



Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice posted on social media: “I told you all.. it’s done.” They celebrated amid wild scenes and then lined up for a team picture with a giant cardboard cut out of the Premier League trophy.

‌



Rice had insisted that “it is not done” after Arsenal lost at City last month and clinched it after Pep Guardiola ’s men dropped points at Bournemouth.

Man City can have no excuses - brilliant Arsenal deserve to win Premier League title READ MORE :

It means a heartbreaking farewell for Guardiola with the City boss preparing to leave the Etihad after ten years in charge after Sunday’s final home game to Aston Villa.

Guardiola sent his congratulations to his former assistant Arteta who has led Arsenal to their first title in 22 years. He said: “Congratulations to Mikel, congratulations to Arsenal, they have been phenomenal.

‌



“We were close. On behalf of everyone at Manchester City, we congratulate Mikel and all the staff, players and fans on winning the Premier League. They deserve it.”

View 3 Images Arsenal players celebrated winning the title at the club's training ground

But Guardiola refused to reveal his future plans and added: “I have one more year of my contract. I will talk to the chairman at the end of the season.

‌



“I will not tell you here – I have to talk to my chairman, my players and my staff.I’m the happiest man in the world to be at this extraordinary club.

View 3 Images Arsenal have won the title for the first time in 22 years

Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has led his club into Europe as his parting gift and said: “At the beginning of the season you didn't imagine it. It has been so nice and we have a chance to fight for the Champions League in the last game and we really deserve this, especially for the game we played so well.

“We have not won the game but it does not matter."I've enjoyed it so much, how we played and the personality we showed. We had great chances to score the second one and we wanted to win the game but I've enjoyed it.”

Sports.title: Arsenal players and staff go wild as they finally win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Arsenal players and staff go wild as they finally win Premier League title

Arsenal were crowned Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years after Manchester City were held to a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth on Tuesday night

View 5 Images Arsenal's players and staff celebrate after being crowned Premier League champions

Arsenal’s players have been celebrating at their Sobha Realty Training Centre after being crowned Premier League champions. The Gunners were officially confirmed as champions after Manchester City were held to a 1-1 draw by Bournemouth on Tuesday night.

‌



City needed to win at Vitality Stadium to take the title race to the final day, but they were unable to force a winner after Erling Haaland equalised in added time. Arsenal’s players and staff gathered together at the club’s training ground to watch the action on the South Coast unfold.

‌



And no sooner had the full-time whistle sounded at the Vitality Stadium, Arsenal’s players and staff celebrated wildly after their status as champions was confirmed. In footage shared by the club, a number of Mikel Arteta’s side could be seen jumping up and down.

‌



View 5 Images Declan Rice and Leandro Trossard celebrate (Image: (Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

While some members broke into small groups and could be seen embracing. However, they were all soon jumping up and down, singing, "Campeones, Campeones, Ole Ole Ole".

Members of the Arsenal squad also posed for a photograph with a cardboard cutout of the Premier League trophy. The Gunners will be presented with the real thing following their game against Crystal Palace on Sunday.

‌



Declan Rice delivers perfect message as Arsenal players celebrate winning title READ MORE :

Man City can have no excuses - brilliant Arsenal deserve to win Premier League title READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Declan Rice posted a picture on Instagram with his team-mates with the caption “I told you all.. it’s done.” While former Gunners boss Arsene Wenger, who led the team to their last title, in 2004, featured in a celebratory post on social media.

View 5 Images Arsenal's players celebrate with a cardboard Premier League title (Image: (Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

‌



He said: “You did it. Champions go on when others stop. This is your time. Now, go on and enjoy every moment.”

Former Gunners goalkeeper David Seaman, said on X: “Premier League champions!!! What a moment!!! What a season!!!!!!!! EPIC!!!!!!!!!! Longest (22 years and ) three minutes of MY LIFE…”

View 5 Images Riccard Calafiori, Piero Hincapie and Noni Madueke celebrate Arsenal winning the Premer League title (Image: (Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

‌



Man City boss Pep Guardiola also sent his congratulations to his former assistant Arteta, saying: “Congratulations to Mikel, congratulations to Arsenal, they have been phenomenal.

“We were close. On behalf of everyone at Manchester City, we congratulate Mikel and all the staff, players and fans on winning the Premier League. They deserve it.”

Reacting to Arsenal’s triumph, former Gunners forward Alan Smith said: "Brilliant! Fully deserved. They have had the best defence, they haven't had the best attack, but as an overall unit Mikel Arteta has done incredibly well.

‌



View 5 Images (Image: (Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

"I was very worried about the last-day game at Palace...so pleased!"

Before he added: "You have to have nervy moments when you haven't won it for that long and Arsenal did have them. But hopefully now they can play with freedom. It almost feels that the Champions League final is a free hit now."

Article continues below

They could still make it an historic double for the club as they chase their first Champions League title in the final against Paris St Germain later this month. But the title win ends a six-year period without a trophy and is Arteta’s second major honour in charge after the 2020 FA Cup victory.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger delivers Champions message as Arsenal end 22-year wait
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger delivers Champions message as Arsenal end 22-year wait

Arsenal have been confirmed as Premier League champions with Arsene Wenger sending a message to the Gunners

View Image Arsene Wenger (Image: Arsenal / X)

Arsene Wenger has delivered a congratulatory message to Arsenal following their confirmation as Premier League champions. The Gunners officially won the title on Tuesday night after Manchester City failed to beat Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium.

‌



City were held to a 1-1 draw with the Cherries, with Eli Junior Kroupi’s goal being cancelled out by a strike from Erling Haaland in the closing minutes on the south coast.

‌



As a result, Arsenal now have an unassailable four-point lead over City going into the final match of the season on Sunday, where the Gunners will travel to face Crystal Palace.

‌



After Arsenal were confirmed as Premier League champions, the Gunners posted a video on their official X account, which included a message from Wenger.

Man City can have no excuses - brilliant Arsenal deserve to win Premier League title READ MORE :

Declan Rice delivers perfect message as Arsenal players celebrate winning title READ MORE :

Wenger, the last manager to win the Premier League title with Arsenal, delivered a clear message of congratulations to Mikel Arteta and the Gunners.

“You did it. Champions go on when others stop,” Wenger said.

‌



“This is your time. Now, go on and enjoy every moment.”

Arsenal’s title win is the club’s first in 22 years, with Wenger guiding the Gunners to the famous Invincible title victory back in 2004.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Arsenal will now face Crystal Palace on Sunday at Selhurst Park, where Arteta and Co. will lift the trophy as champions.

Arteta spoke to the Arsenal home crowd after the 1-0 win over Burnley on Monday night, on what proved to be the eve of the club’s confirmation as Premier League champions.

“It is an absolute joy to witness the transformation and contribution each of you have had to turn this place into the most beautiful place to enjoy and play our football games,” Arteta said.

‌



“This is the soul of this football club. Make sure that every time you step in this stadium you have the responsibility to keep these standards because it makes such a difference to us and the players.”

The Gunners also have a chance to add another trophy to their collection this season, with the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest on the horizon later this month.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta was among those to applaud Rice's comments. Speaking at the time, he said: “It’s not done, and we are more confident that we’re going to do it.

Sports.title: Man City can have no excuses - brilliant Arsenal deserve to win Premier League title
Sports.content:
Man City can have no excuses - brilliant Arsenal deserve to win Premier League title

BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 MAN CITY: Pep Guardiola's side have missed the chance to take the title race to the final day of what will be his final season in charge

View 4 Images Pep Guardiola looks set to leave the Premier League without a title in his final season (Image: Getty Images)

You could almost hear Arsenal’s celebrations down on the South Coast. Manchester City could not give Pep Guardiola a dream leaving present and instead Bournemouth gift-wrapped the title for Arsenal.

‌



There was no fairytale ending for Guardiola as City could not muster one last heroic effort for the greatest manager their club has ever seen.

‌



Guardiola will have to settle for just the two trophies this season - the Carabao Cup and FA Cup to make it 20 pieces of silverware in 10 glorious years - as Arsenal scooped the biggest prize of all.

‌



It has been an incredible race as the rivals have gone toe-to-toe but finally Arsenal have got the better of City. The away fans chanted: “One more year, one more year Guardiola.” But it was all in vain.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta and his players will have watched on, urging Bournemouth to finish the job for them. And that is exactly what they did.

Arsenal Premier League champions - special edition on sale now After 22 years of near-misses, heartbreak and drama, the Gooners are once again the best team in the land. Our souvenir edition tells the story of what has been an extraordinary season by Mikel Arteta's men. Order your copy here

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arteta and his players have earned the champagne and celebrations after the greatest night in 22 years as they finally ended the long wait to be crowned champions.

City gave everything, as they dug deep for one last heroic effort to at least take the title race until the final day and the chance to give Guardiola a dream send off on the final day.

‌



But it was not to be. For once, City were outrun, out-passed and out-pressed. Bournemouth produced an incredible performance as they are chasing their own Champions League dream.

View 4 Images Arsenal fans can finally celebrate (Image: Johnny Goldsmith)

Erling Haaland equalised deep into injury time but by then it was too little too late. The title had gone.

‌



It was Guardiola who said before kick-off that all the talk - and the worst kept secret that he will leave in the summer - was not a distraction and it had “absolutely zero” effect on his team’s preparations.

Surely it did. Surely these City players would have been even motivated to win for their departing manager. But, ultimately, even super heroes run out of energy.

City won the FA Cup at Wembley on Saturday and it was one hell of an ask to come to Bournemouth just three days later. It was win-or-bust - and City could not produce another miracle. Three games in seven days was too much even for City.

‌



Guardiola went over to the away fans at the final whistle but he and the rest of the City players looked shell-shocked. They were outplayed.

View 4 Images Arsenal have been crowned as champions for the first time since 2004 (Image: Johnny Goldsmith)

Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch in Alex Scott as the midfielder ran the show, dictated the pace and set the tempo. It would be unforgivable if England do not take him to the World Cup.

‌



It was Scott who started the move for Bournemouth’s 39th minute goal. Marcus Tavernier took over, Adrien Truffert raced down the left and then his wonderful pull back found Junior Kroupi who curled a shot into the top corner.

Arsenal have been admirers of Kroupi - and now you can bet they like him even more. City were terrific in spells as they pinned Bournemouth back but they have been inconsistent away from home this season and been undone by losing gas in the second half.

View 4 Images Erling Haaland's late goal was mere consolation (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Try as they might, City just could not turn it around. Guardiola threw on Rayan Cherki, Savinho, Phil Foden and Omar Marmoush but even the cavalry could not save City this time.

Haaland got an equaliser in the fifth minute of injury time as City’s never-say-die spirit lives on. Rodri hit the post and then Haaland fired in the rebound. But it was too little too late.

But there should be no excuses. They finished runners-up to Arsenal and they are very worthy champions. Last month, Arsenal lost at Etihad and surrendered top spot only to come again and win the title. Any team that sees off the might of City and Guardiola really deserves it.

Sports.title: Arsenal win Premier League title after Man City slip-up as Gunners end 22-year wait
Sports.content:
Arsenal win Premier League title after Man City slip-up as Gunners end 22-year wait

Manchester City had to beat Bournemouth in order to take the Premier League title race down to the final day, but Pep Guardiola's side have handed Arsenal the trophy with one match to spare

View 4 Images Arsenal players celebrated winning the title at the club's training ground

The wait is finally over. Arsenal have been crowned Premier League champions for the first time in 22 years after Manchester City's 1-1 draw with Bournemouth

‌



City's failure to win at the Vitality Stadium on Tuesday means that Pep Guardiola's men can no longer catch Arsenal when the final round of fixtures takes place this weekend. The Gunners, who've been top of the table for the vast majority of this season, beat Burnley 1-0 on Monday to build a five-point gap between themselves and City.

‌



Kai Havertz's first-half goal made the difference against a Burnley side who've already been relegated. That put the pressure back on City to take all three points from their game in hand at Bournemouth.

‌



The fixture took took 24 hours after the bombshell news broke that Guardiola will be leaving City at the end of the season, despite having one year left on his contract. Eli Junior Kroupi gave Bournemouth the lead in the 39th minute which meant that City needed to score twice.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Arsenal fans shell out £10,000 for vital Crystal Palace tie to see Gunners lift Premier League trophy READ MORE :

Arsenal sweating on Jurrien Timber injury as Mikel Arteta gets worrying update READ MORE :

The visitors were markedly improved after Guardiola made a triple substitution before the hour mark, giving them fresh attacking impetus through the likes of Rayan Cherki. But Bournemouth defended resolutely until the dying embers, as they have done all season under departing boss Andoni Iraola.

‌



The Cherries knew that a victory would put them within a point of fifth-placed Liverpool going into the final day, dreaming of Champions League football. But after Erling Haaland smashed home an equaliser deep into stoppage time, they'll likely have to settle for the Europa League - still a huge milestone.

For City, however, it was too little too late, and the title race is now over. Ninety three miles north, Arsenal fans packed out the Tollington Arms pub near the Emirates to watch on.

Their celebrations will go long into the night after enduring more than two decades of pain. Arsenal's players also watched the match together, knowing that they'll lift the trophy following Sunday's trip to Crystal Palace.

‌



View 4 Images Arsenal went to the Emirates to celebrate (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

View 4 Images Arsenal fans celebrate winning the title outside the Emirates Stadium

After the final whistle on the south coast, Mikel Arteta sent a message to those jubilant supporters: "We made history again together, I cannot be happier and prouder for everybody that is involved in this football club. Let's enjoy the moment."

‌



Arsenal previously won the title in 2004 under legendary manager Arsene Wenger. But Arteta has finally ended the club's long wait after three successive second-placed finishes.

The Gunners began this season with intent, dropping points in just two of their first 10 fixtures. Their solid form continued over the winter before hopes of an historic quadruple quickly evaporated in the spring.

Either side of the international break, Arsenal went on a run of two wins from seven games in all competitions, including a damaging 2-1 defeat away to City which blew the title race wide open. But the Gunners responded with four wins in a row while capitalising on City's 3-3 draw at Everton.

‌



View 4 Images Arsenal legend Ian Wright joins in the celebrations outside the Emirates

Arsenal also reached the Champions League final for only the second time in their history after beating Atletico Madrid 2-1 on aggregate. Arteta's side will face holders Paris Saint-Germain next Saturday in Budapest.

The Spaniard was appointed to replace Unai Emery in December 2019, taking on his first managerial role after working under Guardiola at City. Having lifted the FA Cup in Arteta's first season during the pandemic, the league title also ends Arsenal's six-year wait for a trophy.

Article continues below

City, on the other hand, will finish what's expected to be Guardiola's 10th and final season at the helm with two trophies. His team won the FA Cup on Saturday, having previously beaten Arsenal in March's Carabao Cup final.

Image: Arsenal were invincible in their 2003/04 campaign

It has been a long wait for the red side of north London.

Arsenal last won the Premier League title back in the 2003/04 season when Arsene Wenger's side went through the whole league season unbeaten.

It was the third title of the Wenger era but a special one as the Gunners secured 26 wins and 12 draws on their way to becoming the Invincibles.

Image: Arsenal last lifted the Premier League trophy in 2004

Sports.title: Man City's title bid over as Bournemouth draw sees Arsenal crowned champions
Sports.content:
Manchester City's hopes of winning the Premier League title are over after a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth saw Arsenal crowned champions.

Eli Junior Kroupi's curling first-half effort helped give the Gunners a first Premier League title in 22 years, and despite Erling Haaland's late leveller - it means Pep Guardiola has gone without the league title in back-to-back seasons for the first time in his managerial career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eli Junior Kroupi fires Bournemouth in front against Man City!

The result also ensured Bournemouth will be playing European football next season, an achievement secured in head coach Andoni Iraola's final home match in charge before his departure.

With Guardiola expected to leave City after the season, City fans still called for him to stay from the away end. They also sang: "We'll fight to the end" - but Bournemouth made sure that fight will not be carried into Sunday's final day.

City had some half chances in the first half, with Jeremy Doku forcing Djorde Petrovic into a good save early on, but rarely troubled the Cherries.

Player ratings: Bournemouth: Petrovic (8); Smith (7), Hill (8), Senesi (8), Truffert (8); Adams (7), Tavernier (7), Scott (6); Rayan (7), Evanilson (7), Kroupi (8)



Subs: Kluivert (6), Brooks (4), Unal (n/a), Cook (n/a)



Man City: Donnarumma (7); Nunes (6), Khusanov (5), Guehi (6), O’Reilly (6); Rodri (7), Kovacic (6), Bernardo (6); Semenyo (5), Haaland (7), Doku (7)



Subs: Foden (5), Cherki (5), Savinho (5), Marmoush (6)



Player of the Match: Eli Junior Kroupi

At the other end, Evanilson missed a glaring chance from six yards out with the goal gaping - with only the offside flag sparing his blushes.

Then came the first half's big moment as Adrien Truffert broke down the left and cut the ball back to Kroupi, who left Gianluigi Donnarumma rooted to the spot by finding the top corner.

Guardiola needed a response and it nearly came seconds into the second half - but Petrovic managed to deny Nico O'Reilly when the City defender was played through.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico O'Reilly was denied by Djordje Petrovic as Bournemouth survived a scare early in the second half!

After City brought on Rayan Cherki, Phil Foden and Savinho in an attacking move, Bournemouth got more joy at the other end. Kroupi curled over a good chance from the edge of the box, before Rayan hit the post from close range at a corner.

But despite more City pressure, Bournemouth looked mostly likely to get a second as David Brooks missed two golden chances to seal the game - including hitting the post when clean through.

Haaland equalised in the final minute after Rodri hit the post. But the final whistle sparked jubilant scenes in Dorset and the red half of north London. It looks like all Guardiola has in Sunday's final game with Aston Villa is a farewell bow.

Pep reacts to conceding title - and will he stay?

Image: Pep Guardiola shows his frustration as Manchester City's Premier League hopes end with the draw at Bournemouth

Man City manager Pep Guardiola:

"Expanding on his response over his future in the post-match press conference, Guardiola added: "Listen, with the club, always I talk, but not now.

"The first thing you have to understand is you should talk with my chairman first, right? And after that, when I talk with my chairman, we'll decide.

When asked if the talks will come after their final match of the season on Sunday, Guardiola said: "No, no, we'll talk the next few days.

"Always we talk with my chairman. What are we going to do, what are we not going to do. But I think he [the chairman] deserves [to be the first one spoken to], right?

On whether Sunday's match will be his last at City, he added: "Let me talk about my chairman! I know they [the fans] love me so much. I love them more. I know that it's the best place to be. I love that place [the Etihad]. I adore it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester City players and Arsenal fans reacted to the Gunners sealing the Premier League title after Man City's 1-1 draw with Bournemouth.

"Let me talk about my club. Even though people say I talk to a thousand million people in person, I was incredibly, incredibly focused on my job. When we are in the competitions, I'm there. I was there. This is what I have to do."

Iraola: I'm not sure where I will go

Bournemouth head coach Andoni Iraola to Sky Sports:

"At the beginning of the season you didn't imagine [Europe]. It has been so nice and we have a chance to fight for the Champions League in the last game and we really deserve this, especially for the game we played so well. We have not won the game but it does not matter.

"Today has been a good reflection of the club. I'm very happy for the club, the players, the supporters and the staff. It's the best way to finish with something you can touch I can't ask for anything more.

"Pep is the top of the top. He has won everything. It was a difficult game for them, they played three days ago with the tension of a final. We made them play a difficult game and they were obviously tired but they have this quality. It makes it even more nice when you play like this against an opposition that are so good.

"We have a special group of players. They are consistent and always there. Right now there is nothing about my future in my head, I just want to celebrate and push it. We have Europa League, next let's maximise our options. Can we take the last Champions League spot?

"I still don't know where I will go but I'm in no rush, let's finish on a high."

Richards: Guardiola the greatest manager of his generation

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following the 1-1 draw with Bournemouth in the Premier League, Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola remained coy on his future at the club and told Sky Sports that he will talk to the chairman at the end of the season.

Former Man City defender Micah Richards on Sky Sports:

"He is the greatest manager of his generation without doubt and I say that because of the way he plays football. There are certain ways you can win a football match.

"Arteta and Arsenal have done it a little bit more defensively. But in terms of his 10-year tenure at Man City, whether it's full-backs inverted, false nines, playing (John) Stones in central midfield in the Champions League final, he has just created a way to love the game and for the game to be played in the right way."
